teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji hold captain's run at Kirwan Park, not the Aviva
teams.body: Fiji have trained at De La Salle Palmerston FC, the junior club known locally as 'Salmo', this week, and the squad has become part of the furniture. Their captain's run on Friday will be at Kirwan Park rather than the Aviva Stadium, and non-playing squad members train there again on Saturday morning. Forwards coach Gert Smal, once of Ireland, is watching the sessions with a keen eye. DLSP FC director of rugby Norman Byrne says: "They're the nicest people you'll ever come across."

lead.why: It is the freshest Fiji-specific item on the shortlist, and it is not a rewrite of the France defeat or the Ireland team news that already ran.

teams.heading: Borthwick restores Max Ojomoh to England's No. 12 shirt against Japan
teams.body: Bath centre Max Ojomoh is back in England's No. 12 shirt after starring for the A team, having not played for his country since his man-of-the-match display against Argentina a year ago. England head coach Steve Borthwick says the position now demands more than skill: "Max is one of the most talented players in English rugby," he said. Fly-half George Ford returns to the starting side, with Fin Smith left out.

lead.why: Borthwick's selection of Max Ojomoh at 12 is a fresh England team decision, and the BBC piece carries the coach's own words on it.

teams.heading: Galthié keeps Marcoussis camp closed to media before Springboks test
teams.body: Marc Duzan of Rugbyrama reports that Rassie Erasmus, Springboks head coach, named his side on Monday, while France's Marcoussis camp this week was run behind closed doors with the press kept out. Duzan calls that almost unprecedented for Fabien Galthié, France head coach. Rugbyrama's request for an interview was refused, with the reply: "C’est pas le bon moment."

lead.why: It is a new France-side story about Galthié's closed training camp and refused media access, and it is not a rerun of the Dupont, Desperes/Le Brun or Kolisi items already published.

teams.heading: James Ryan insists Ireland are not thinking about South Africa yet
teams.body: James Ryan, who returns to the starting XV at lock alongside Tadhg Beirne, has played down talk of next Saturday's clash with the world champions. Speaking to RTÉ Sport, he said: "We're not thinking about South Africa," adding, "I know that's the boring answer, but it is the answer." Last year's 24-13 Dublin defeat to the Springboks, in which Ryan received a 20-minute red card, gives the fixture extra edge. He also wants Ireland to build on the 42-12 win over Argentina.

lead.why: It is the only new item in the shortlist, and it is a direct quote from an Ireland player on the Springboks test that follows Fiji.

teams.heading: Captain Giacomo Nicotera admits Italy gave away too many penalties against Sudafrica
teams.body: Italy captain Giacomo Nicotera said the team was very critical of its performance after the 7-66 defeat to South Africa, which he called not sufficient. The review covered aerial play, defence, organisation and discipline, with too many penalties partly caused by South Africa's pressure at the breakdown. Nicotera described a hard review on Monday and a more demanding week in training. Ahead of Saturday's test against Argentina in Genoa, he said winning their own ball would be fundamental to getting more attacking possession.

lead.why: It is a new, first-hand captain's review of the South Africa defeat, ahead of today's match, and it is about Italy's own performance.

teams.heading: Gregor Townsend recalls Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn against Australia on Sunday
teams.body: Two changes to Scotland's XV for Sunday's Nations Championship test with Australia at Murrayfield. Kinghorn takes the full-back jersey from Kyle Rowe, who is not in the squad, while Graham, 29, is on the left wing after a quicker-than-expected recovery from a bicep tear. Townsend has stressed "individual responsibility" after Scotland conceded seven tries in a 21-43 defeat to New Zealand. Ollie Leatherbarrow, who qualifies through his grandmother from Perth, could make his debut off the bench.

lead.why: It is a new Scotland team announcement with Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn back in the XV, which is the story a fan would text a mate about.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy starts Taine Basham at eight, Gabriel Hamer-Webb on left wing
teams.body: Wales head coach Steve Tandy has made four changes to his starting line-up for Saturday's clash with New Zealand. Taine Basham moves into the number eight jersey, Gabriel Hamer-Webb takes the left wing, James Botham comes in at blindside flanker and Adam Beard comes in at lock. The shake-up follows a 28-21 win over Japan last weekend, a match still in the balance until its closing stages. New Zealand have won 34 games in a row against Wales since the 1953 win.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item that names Wales's changed starting XV for this match, and it is not the Beard recall already reported on 12 November.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi, under fire over results, says doing things well brings wins
teams.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi faces a fierce wave of criticism over results, including a win over Wales bracketed by heavy home defeats to Scotland and England. Ahead of Italy, he says he wants the win first, but that the route to it is doing things well in the week. Winning is the goal, he said, yet the team can only control its own preparation. Argentina's last outing was a 42-12 defeat to Ireland.

lead.why: Contepomi's pre-match press conference answers a fresh wave of criticism of his coaching, and the fan will want his response.

teams.heading: Les Kiss restores Carter Gordon at fly-half, moves Suaalii to centre
teams.body: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has made three changes and two positional switches for the Scotland test at Murrayfield. Gordon replaces Declan Meredith at fly-half, returning from a fractured leg sustained in the 28-28 draw with Argentina in Mendoza in September. Joseph Suaalii, who has played on the wing in Australia's last four Tests, moves back to outside centre alongside Len Ikitau, replacing Isaac Henry. Rob Valetini is back in the starting XV on the blindside flank.

lead.why: It is the newest item on the sheet and a direct Wallabies selection call for the Scotland test.

teams.heading: Japan face Max Ojomoh and Henry Pollock as Borthwick rings the changes
teams.body: England head coach Steve Borthwick is ringing the changes for Japan, and the Guardian's Robert Kitson picks out Max Ojomoh as the standout case. Ojomoh, 26, has not played for England since being voted player of the match against Argentina a year ago, and Kitson writes he would probably not be back at 12 without injuries to Seb Atkinson and Benhard van Rensburg. Henry Pollock, who scored two tries from the wing against Australia, is listed at No 8, though Kitson suggests his role could change.

lead.why: It is the only NEW shortlist item, and its selection news on Ojomoh and Pollock sets the tone for the match Japan are about to play.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie names Beauden Barrett All Blacks captain, Scott Barrett passed over
teams.body: Utility back Beauden Barrett captains the All Blacks in Cardiff, the first time the 148-Test player has skippered his country at Test level. New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie passed over Scott Barrett, the first-choice captain in 2024 and 2025, who starts at lock. Rennie said: "I don't think he needs the extra responsibility," adding that Scott Barrett will be closer to the action and should talk to the referee where possible. Codie Taylor had captained after Ardie Savea's shoulder injury.

lead.why: A new selection call that names the captain and passes over a former first-choice skipper, which a fan would talk about before kickoff.

teams.heading: Siya Kolisi says Springboks have no special plans for Antoine Dupont switch
teams.body: Springboks captain Siya Kolisi told reporters on Thursday that South Africa's defensive structures will not change for France's Antoine Dupont, who has been selected at fly-half. "Our system doesn't change for any team we play against," Kolisi said. Assistant coach Mzawandile Stick has confirmed the Boks have made no special plans to limit him, and Kolisi and Stick predict Dupont and scrum-half Maxime Lucu will job share throughout, both having played fly-half for their clubs.

lead.why: It is a new item in which the Springboks captain sets out South Africa's own plan for France's fly-half change, ahead of the next Test.
